outroLine: Test, publish, and roll back with confidence.

beats.shot: Land on /connections: the list shows each supplier connection with its lifecycle badge (Published / Draft).
beats.vo: A connection is everything one supplier integration is — the input mapping, the output template, delivery, and item codes — bundled together and versioned, like releases of software.

beats.shot: Click into FastParts Inc: the Live revision card — what this supplier receives for new orders today, and the immutability note.
beats.vo: Opening one shows the live revision — exactly what this supplier receives for new orders today. Published revisions are immutable. Nobody can quietly change what production does.

beats.shot: Cursor moves to the Revision history: v2 draft with Run tests / Publish, v1 published and live.
beats.vo: Changing anything means a draft. The history shows every version of this connection and where it is in its life. Draft, published, archived.

beats.shot: Cursor clicks 'Run tests' on the v2 draft; the test-pack evidence appears inline (replay over recent orders + conformance).
beats.vo: Run tests replays your own recent orders through the draft and checks the output against the supplier's conformance profile. Nothing is delivered. It's evidence, before you commit.

beats.shot: Scroll to 'Replay & impact preview'; click Run replay; the per-order diff list appears — output changed, validation changed, would start failing.
beats.vo: The impact preview goes further. Replay recent orders and see, order by order, what would change — including orders that pass today but would start failing under the draft. You see the blast radius before you publish.

beats.shot: Scroll back up; click Publish on v2; the confirm dialog explains in-flight orders keep their revision; confirm; the success notice lands and v1 flips to archived.
beats.vo: Publishing flips the draft live for new orders. And orders already in flight keep the revision they were created with. That is the reproducibility guarantee — you can always say exactly which rules produced any order.

beats.shot: Cursor rests on 'Roll back to this' on the now-archived v1.
beats.vo: And if a publish turns out wrong, the previous version is one click away. Rollback republishes it as a new revision. History is never rewritten.
